import { existsSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync, mkdirSync, statSync } from 'node:fs'
import { resolve, join, extname } from 'node:path'
import { createHash } from 'node:crypto'
import { createServer } from 'node:http'
import { spawn } from 'node:child_process'
import { pathToFileURL } from 'node:url'
import { child } from './session-lifecycle.mjs'
import { livePreviewScript, watchProject } from './live-preview.mjs'

export function projectType(root) {
  if (existsSync(join(root, 'package.json'))) {
    const p = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(root, 'package.json'), 'utf8'))
    if (p.dependencies?.next || p.devDependencies?.next) throw new Error('Unsupported framework: customize start.sh and provide static deployment output.')
    if (p.dependencies?.vite || p.devDependencies?.vite) return 'vite'
    throw new Error('Unsupported package project: customize start.sh and deployment output.')
  }
  if (existsSync(join(root, 'index.html'))) return 'html'
  throw new Error('No generated index.html or supported package project.')
}
export async function start(root = process.cwd()) {
  const type = projectType(root)
  const projectRoot = resolve(root)
  if (type === 'vite') {
    const stampDir = process.env.OPENCODE_WEB_DIR || join(root, 'node_modules', '.cache')
    mkdirSync(stampDir, { recursive: true })
    const stamp = join(stampDir, 'default-dependencies')
    const lock = join(root, 'package-lock.json')
    const hash = createHash('sha256').update(readFileSync(join(root, 'package.json'))).update(existsSync(lock) ? readFileSync(lock) : '').digest('hex')
    let old = ''
    try { old = readFileSync(stamp, 'utf8') } catch {}
    if (old !== hash || !existsSync(join(root, 'node_modules/vite'))) {
      await child('npm', [existsSync(lock) ? 'ci' : 'install', '--no-audit', '--no-fund'], { cwd: root })
      mkdirSync(stampDir, { recursive: true })
      const installedHash = createHash('sha256').update(readFileSync(join(root, 'package.json'))).update(existsSync(lock) ? readFileSync(lock) : '').digest('hex')
      writeFileSync(stamp, installedHash)
    }
    await child(process.execPath, [join(root, 'node_modules/vite/bin/vite.js'), 'build', '--base', './'], { cwd: root })
    root = join(root, 'dist')
  }
  if (!existsSync(join(root, 'index.html'))) throw new Error('Static deployment output must contain index.html.')
  if (process.env.OPENCODE_WEB_DIR) writeFileSync(join(process.env.OPENCODE_WEB_DIR, 'deployment-output.json'), JSON.stringify({ project: projectRoot, directory: resolve(root) }))
  const mime = { '.html':'text/html', '.js':'application/javascript', '.css':'text/css', '.json':'application/json', '.svg':'image/svg+xml', '.png':'image/png', '.jpg':'image/jpeg', '.webp':'image/webp', '.wasm':'application/wasm', '.glb':'model/gltf-binary' }
  const clients = new Set()
  const stopWatching = watchProject(root, () => { for (const client of clients) client.write('event: change\ndata: changed\n\n') })
  const keepAlive = setInterval(() => { for (const client of clients) client.write(': keepalive\n\n') }, 20000)
  const buildWatcher = type === 'vite' ? spawn(process.execPath, [join(projectRoot, 'node_modules/vite/bin/vite.js'), 'build', '--base', './', '--watch'], { cwd: projectRoot, stdio: 'inherit' }) : null
  const server = createServer((req, res) => {
    try {
      const url = new URL(req.url, 'http://localhost')
      if (url.pathname === '/__omgithub/live') {
        res.writeHead(200, { 'Content-Type': 'text/event-stream', 'Cache-Control': 'no-cache', 'X-Accel-Buffering': 'no', Connection: 'keep-alive' })
        res.write(': connected\n\n')
        clients.add(res)
        req.on('close', () => clients.delete(res))
        return
      }
      const path = resolve(root, '.' + decodeURIComponent(url.pathname))
      if (path !== resolve(root) && !path.startsWith(resolve(root) + '/')) { res.writeHead(404); res.end(); return }
      const file = statSync(path).isDirectory() ? join(path, 'index.html') : path
      res.setHeader('Content-Type', mime[extname(file)] || 'application/octet-stream')
      res.setHeader('Cache-Control', url.searchParams.has('omgithub_live') ? 'no-store' : 'no-cache')
      const content = readFileSync(file)
      if (extname(file) === '.html' && url.searchParams.get('omgithub_live') === '1') {
        const html = content.toString()
        res.end(/<\/body\s*>/i.test(html) ? html.replace(/<\/body\s*>/i, `${livePreviewScript}</body>`) : html + livePreviewScript)
      } else res.end(content)
    } catch { res.writeHead(404); res.end('Not found') }
  })
  server.on('close', () => { stopWatching(); clearInterval(keepAlive); buildWatcher?.kill(); for (const client of clients) client.end() })
  server.listen(Number(process.env.PORT || 3000), '0.0.0.0')
  return server
}

So it's a static HTML project. I need to build a complete mobile game with index.html. Let me plan the game. Game concept: "Phone Repair Shop" mobile game. Each day a customer comes in with a phone problem. You need to perform the repair via touch gestures: - Cracked screen → peel off cracked glass (swipe/drag), unscrew, place new screen - Dead battery → open back panel, remove battery, insert new battery - Water damage → dry with towel/blower, clean ports - Broken charging port → clean/desolder and replace - Camera broken → replace camera module - Speaker issue → replace speaker Must be mobile-first, no scrolling. Full viewport, touch controls, drag gestures. Design considerations: 1. Portrait mobile game, fixed viewport 390x844-ish, but responsive to fill screen. 2. Touch-based drag interaction, not scrolling. `touch-action: none`, `overscroll-behavior: none`, `user-select: none`, fixed body. 3. Art: CSS/SVG-drawn phone in top-down view. I want it to look good — clean UI, workbench background, phone lying on a mat. 4. Repair loop: - Customer arrives with dialogue bubble describing issue. - Diagnosis: choose correct tool/part? Maybe simpler: each repair is a sequence of touch actions. - Actions: a. **Screen replacement**: swipe over cracked screen to peel shards (e.g., drag across 6 crack segments), then tap to lift old screen off, then drag new screen from tray to the phone, then press it in (tap/hold progress). b. **Battery**: swipe along the seam to release back panel, then swipe the adhesive, tap to lift battery, drag new battery into slot, press to connect. c. **Charging port**: use brush/dust blower (swipe in port), then unscrew 4 screws by tapping, drag new port, press. d. **Speaker**: unscrew, lift speaker, drag new speaker, press. e. **Water damage**: drag towel across phone to dry, then open & clean with brush, then press. - Then finalize: tap "Done" or press power button and see if it boots. 5. Scoring: time, accuracy, customer satisfaction; money earned; day counter; shop upgrades maybe. 6. Feedback: haptics (navigator.vibrate), sounds via WebAudio (no external assets), particles. Complexity vs robustness: Need it to be genuinely playable and visually convincing. I'll implement a generic repair-step engine: Repair job = list of steps. Each step type: - `swipe`: drag along a path / fill a progress meter by swiping across a specified zone. For "peel screen" - rub progress across the area. Visual: cracked layer's opacity reduces per progress; glass shards fly. - `tap`: tap N targets (screws) — each tap shows screw rotating out. Or tap a single target to lift component. - `drag`: drag a part from the parts tray into the phone slot; snap when within threshold. Used for new screen/battery. - `hold`: press and hold on a spot to seat/connect (progress ring). That's a nice variety with simple mechanics that work with mobile touch. Also add "wrong tool" choice? Maybe skip to keep frustration low, but "based on problem is what you need to do" is covered by different step sequences. Could add a tool selection strip: tools: pry tool, screwdriver, spudger, suction cup... Each step requires the right tool selected before performing. Hmm, that adds gameplay depth and is thematic. But could add frustration on mobile. I could implement tool auto-required: the current step shows "Use: Pry Tool" and you must select from bottom toolbar, then act. That's a nice loop: select tool → perform action. Perhaps include for some steps only; simpler: every step declares a tool, and tool bar highlights. Selecting the wrong tool shows a shake + hint "That won't help here". Since each day's repair is different and tools differ, adds decision-making. I think a good compromise: the toolbar has tools that matter: Suction cup, Pry pick, Screwdriver (torx), Spudger, Brush, Heat gun. Steps specify tool. Auto-select the needed tool for first step? No — require player to choose; it's the "what you need to do" part. Add gentle hint after 4s idle. Hmm, actually requiring tool selection before each action may slow the flow. But it makes the game a game rather than following prompts. I'll include it but make it forgiving: tapping action zone with wrong tool just rattles. Let me think about scope/time. import { startForCapture } from './capture-start.mjs'
import captures from './wip-screenshots.cjs'
import { createRequire } from 'node:module'
import { readFileSync, mkdirSync } from 'node:fs'
import { join } from 'node:path'
const runtime = join(process.env.HOME, '.local/share/omgithub-playwright')
const require = createRequire(join(runtime, 'package.json'))
const { chromium } = require('playwright')
captures.instrument({ chromium })
const config = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(runtime, process.platform === 'darwin' ? 'metal.json' : 'linux.json'), 'utf8'))
if (process.platform === 'linux') process.env.DISPLAY ||= ':' + readFileSync(join(runtime, 'display'), 'utf8').trim()
const url = process.env.CAPTURE_URL, output = process.env.CAPTURE_DIR
if (!url || !output) throw new Error('Set CAPTURE_URL and CAPTURE_DIR.')
mkdirSync(output, { recursive: true })
const transient = error => { throw Object.assign(error, { exitCode: 75 }) }
let browser
try {
  browser = await chromium.launch({ ...config.browser.launchOptions, timeout: 30000 }).catch(transient)
  for (const [name, width, height] of [['desktop', 1440, 900], ['mobile', 390, 844]]) {
    const page = await browser.newPage({ viewport: { width, height } }).catch(transient)
    page.setDefaultTimeout(30000)
    const failures = []
    page.on('pageerror', error => { console.error(error.message); failures.push(error.message) })
    page.on('response', response => { if (response.status() >= 400 && new URL(response.url()).origin === new URL(url).origin) failures.push(`HTTP ${response.status()}: ${response.url()}`) })
    const response = await page.goto(url, { waitUntil: 'load', timeout: 45000 }).catch(transient)
    if (!response?.ok()) throw Object.assign(new Error(`HTTP ${response?.status()} loading preview`), { exitCode: !response || [408, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504].includes(response.status()) ? 75 : 1 })
    await page.locator(process.env.CAPTURE_READY_SELECTOR || 'body').waitFor({ state: 'visible' })
    await page.waitForFunction(() => document.fonts.status === 'loaded')
    const start = await startForCapture(page, {
      enabled: process.env.CAPTURE_AUTO_START !== 'false',
      selector: process.env.CAPTURE_START_SELECTOR || ''
    })
    console.log(`Capture ${name}: auto-start ${start.clicked ? 'clicked' : start.reason}`)
    await page.waitForTimeout(1000)
    await page.screenshot({ path: join(output, `final-${name}.png`), timeout: 30000 }).catch(error => {
      if (error.name === 'TimeoutError' || !browser.isConnected()) transient(error)
      throw error
    })
    if (process.env.CAPTURE_STRICT === '1' && failures.length) throw new Error(`Published build failed: ${failures.join('; ')}`)
    await page.close()
  }
} catch (error) { console.error(error); process.exitCode = error.exitCode || 1 }
finally { await browser?.close().catch(error => { console.error(error); process.exitCode ||= 75 }) }

  const onDown = e=>{
    if(e.button!==undefined && e.button>0) return;

    source.style.visibility='hidden'; // not opacity to keep layout
    dragging=true; moved=0;
    const onMove = ev=>{
      if(!dragging) return;
      const dx=ev.clientX-lastPt.x, dy=ev.clientY-lastPt.y;
      moved += Math.hypot(dx,dy);
      lastPt={x:ev.clientX,y:ev.clientY};

    };
    ...
  };
}

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable mobile-first phone repair shop game with a full shift system and hands-on repair interactions.

## Requirements
- Tailored specifically for portrait mobile players, with no web-style scrolling.
- Daily customer flow with varied phone problems and corresponding repairs.
- Players diagnose the issue, remove/replace components, and complete repairs through touch interactions.
- Include clear progress, rewards, failure, and replay systems.

## Decisions
- Built the game as a single-page vanilla HTML/CSS/JavaScript experience named “MEND.”
- Used a portrait phone-repair shop interface with touch-first drag, screw, rub, heat, hold, and pressure interactions.
- Included local-save support for money, day, reputation, upgrades, sound, and shift progress.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented the main mobile game layout, HUD, customer card, repair bench, tray, diagnosis sheet, payment sheet, menu, and end-of-day flow.
- Added multiple repair jobs and component types: broken screens, batteries, cameras, speakers, charging ports, and boot issues.
- Added step-by-step repairs with screws, dragging, rubbing, heating, scraping, holding, and boot testing.
- Added customer avatars, animation, feedback, toast messages, vibration/audio hooks, stars, pay, tips, reputation, and saves.
- Added responsive portrait orientation handling and a rotate-phone warning.
- Added representative repair and diagnosis screenshots under `screenshots/`.

- (none)

- (none)

1. Continue from the tested repair flow if further polish or testing is requested.
2. Run a final full playthrough across all supported jobs and payment/end-day transitions.
3. Investigate and address any remaining mobile interaction edge cases found during real-device testing.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: Main game markup and UI structure.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/styles.css`: Mobile-first visual system, animations, layout, and responsive rules.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/game.js`: Game state, jobs, repair interactions, save system, audio, customer flow, and payments.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/screenshots/`: Saved JPEG checks for menus and repair states.

## Important Context
- The local server used for visual testing was `python3 -m http.server 3000 --bind 0.0.0.0`.

2. rub cracks: find `.rub-zone`, pointerdown at its center, then ~40 pointermove points in a zigzag across zone, pointerup. Need total 520px; ensure enough movement. Use 30 moves across 300px width maybe 8 passes = 2400px. Wait.
3. dragOut screen: source screenLayer pointerdown, pointermove toward tray in steps, pointerup over tray. Wait.
4. dragIn: mini in tray; drag to phone center. Wait.
5. hold: find `.hold-zone`, pointerdown, wait 1100ms, pointerup. Wait 400.
6. boot: automatic, wait 3s.
Then check pay sheet.

The rub zone may cover the phone but pointerdown on zone; dispatch on zone itself.

For pointermove, listener is on window, so dispatch on window or document. I'll dispatch on window with clientX.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable phone-repair shop game where the player owns the shop, serves customers with varied phone problems, and performs matching repairs.
- Make the game specifically for portrait mobile play, without web-style scrolling.

## Requirements
- Each day brings customers with different phone problems and corresponding repairs, such as replacing a broken screen or failed battery.
- Use touch-friendly, hands-on repair interactions and keep the game playable without page scrolling.
- Build the game now without asking clarifying questions.

## Decisions
- Implemented “MEND” as a single-page vanilla HTML/CSS/JavaScript game.
- Added a daily shift, customer queue, repair payments, upgrades, and local saves.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built the mobile-first game UI, repair interactions, six repair job types, diagnosis, payment, failure, end-of-day, upgrade, and replay flows.
- Tested all six job types to payment using the debug API; verified two-job shift completion, next-day transition, upgrade purchase, and save restoration.
- Saved representative screenshots in `screenshots/`.

### Active
- Validate complete repairs using real touch/pointer interactions; a synthetic pointer test advanced past screws but did not progress through later repair steps, so hands-on interaction remains unverified.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Test the repair interactions in a browser using realistic pointer/touch input and fix any confirmed interaction issues.
2. Run a complete shift through normal play, including payment, failure, end-of-day, and replay.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game markup and UI structure.
- `styles.css`: Mobile-first layout, visual styling, and interaction feedback.
- `game.js`: Game state, job definitions, repair interactions, saves, and shift flow.
- `screenshots/`: Existing repair and UI checks.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- The debug API is exposed as `MEND`; methods include `start()`, `jump(id)`, `correct()`, `skip()`, `failJob()`, `endDay()`, `hint()`, and `reset()`.
- Job IDs tested: `screen`, `battery`, `camera`, `port`, `speaker`, `water`.
- A browser console check only reported missing `favicon.ico` (404).

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable phone-repair shop game for portrait mobile play, where customers bring varied problems and players perform matching repairs.
- Keep gameplay touch-friendly and playable without page scrolling.

## Requirements
- Each day brings customers with different phone problems and corresponding repairs.
- Use hands-on repair interactions and prevent web-style scrolling.
- Build the game without asking clarifying questions.

## Decisions
- Implemented “MEND” as a single-page vanilla HTML/CSS/JavaScript game with daily shifts, customer queues, payments, upgrades, and local saves.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built the mobile-first UI and six repair job types, diagnosis, payment, failure, end-of-day, upgrade, and replay flows.
- Debug-API checks previously verified all six job types to payment, two-job shift completion, next-day transition, upgrade purchase, and save restoration.
- Saved representative UI and repair screenshots in `screenshots/`.

### Active
- Validate complete repairs using realistic pointer/touch interactions and play a full shift, including payment, failure, end-of-day, and replay.
- Latest synthetic pointer test reached screen repair step 4/6 but did not reach payment.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Diagnose why the latest interaction test stopped at screen repair step 4/6; continue validating drag, hold, and boot interactions through payment.
2. Run a complete shift through normal play, including payment, failure, end-of-day, and replay.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game markup and UI structure.
- `styles.css`: Mobile-first layout, visual styling, and interaction feedback.
- `game.js`: Game state, job definitions, repair interactions, saves, and shift flow.
- `/tmp/mend-interaction-test.html`: Temporary browser test harness for pointer-driven repair interactions.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- Debug API: `MEND` methods include `start()`, `jump(id)`, `correct()`, `skip()`, `failJob()`, `endDay()`, `hint()`, and `reset()`.
- Latest test output: `screen: repair at 4/6` followed by `ERROR Error: did not reach payment for screen`; earlier tests verified all six job types to payment using the debug API.
- Browser console previously reported only a missing `favicon.ico` (404).

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable phone-repair shop game for portrait mobile play, with varied customer problems and matching hands-on repairs.
- Keep gameplay touch-friendly and playable without page scrolling.

## Requirements
- Each day brings customers with different phone problems and corresponding repairs.
- Use hands-on repair interactions and prevent web-style scrolling.
- Build the game without asking clarifying questions.

## Decisions
- Implemented “MEND” as a single-page vanilla HTML/CSS/JavaScript game with daily shifts, customer queues, payments, upgrades, and local saves.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built the mobile-first UI and six repair job types, diagnosis, payment, failure, end-of-day, upgrade, and replay flows.
- Debug-API checks verified all six job types to payment, two-job shift completion, next-day transition, upgrade purchase, and save restoration.
- Realistic pointer interactions verified the screen-repair job through payment, including screws, rubbing, dragging, holding, and boot.

### Active
- Validate realistic pointer/touch interactions for the remaining repair types.
- Play a complete shift through payment, failure, end-of-day, and replay.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Validate remaining repair types using realistic pointer interactions through payment.
2. Run a complete shift, including normal payment, failure, end-of-day, and replay.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game markup and UI structure.
- `styles.css`: Mobile-first layout, visual styling, and interaction feedback.
- `game.js`: Game state, job definitions, repair interactions, saves, and shift flow.
- `/tmp/mend-interaction-test.html`: Temporary browser test harness; earlier test stopped at screen step 4/6, but a later WebDriver pointer test completed that repair.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- Debug API: `MEND` methods include `start()`, `jump(id)`, `correct()`, `skip()`, `failJob()`, `endDay()`, `hint()`, and `reset()`.
- The later realistic screen interaction test reached `phase: "pay"` at step `5`; previous interruption at step 4/6 was due to synthetic pointer testing, not a confirmed game defect.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable phone-repair shop game for portrait mobile play, with varied customer problems and matching hands-on repairs.
- Keep gameplay touch-friendly and playable without page scrolling.

## Requirements
- Each day brings customers with different phone problems and corresponding repairs.
- Use hands-on repair interactions and prevent web-style scrolling.
- Build the game without asking clarifying questions.

## Decisions
- Implemented “MEND” as a single-page vanilla HTML/CSS/JavaScript game with daily shifts, customer queues, payments, upgrades, and local saves.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built the mobile-first UI and six repair job types, diagnosis, payment, failure, end-of-day, upgrade, and replay flows.
- Debug-API checks verified all six job types to payment, two-job shift completion, next-day transition, upgrade purchase, and save restoration.
- Realistic pointer interactions verified the screen-repair job through payment.

### Active
- Validate realistic pointer interactions for the remaining repair types.
- Play a complete shift through payment, failure, end-of-day, and replay.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue realistic pointer interaction checks for battery, camera, port, speaker, and water repairs; investigate the latest harness error if it recurs.
2. Run a complete shift, including normal payment, failure, end-of-day, and replay.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game markup and UI structure.
- `styles.css`: Mobile-first layout, visual styling, and interaction feedback.
- `game.js`: Game state, job definitions, repair interactions, saves, and shift flow.
- `/tmp/mend-interaction-test.html`: Temporary browser test harness.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- Debug API: `MEND` methods include `start()`, `jump(id)`, `correct()`, `skip()`, `failJob()`, `endDay()`, `hint()`, and `reset()`.
- The latest realistic interaction attempt stopped on the battery job at step 1 with `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'getBoundingClientRect')` in the test harness’s `rub()` function; it did not confirm a game defect.
